You are verifying a security/architecture hypothesis in this Lobu monorepo (packages/server). This is READ-ONLY analysis: do NOT edit any file, do NOT run any mutation. Answer purely with file:line evidence and a verdict per claim.

CLAIM 1: requireHumanApprovalContext in packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts (around line 2338) rejects any ToolContext carrying agentId OR clientId and requires userId to be present. Quote the exact condition.

CLAIM 2: Because of Claim 1, an ordinary MCP tools/call to manage_operations approve/reject can never pass. Verify how the MCP handler builds ToolContext from an MCP session in packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts (look at how authCtx/clientId/agentId/userId are populated; check the tools/registry.ts ToolContext type). Find whether clientId is ALWAYS non-null for OAuth MCP sessions, and whether agentId is set when the session is bound to an agent. Also check PAT-session handling: is there any MCP session where clientId is null, and if so, does that break the "MCP can never pass" claim? Be precise.

CLAIM 3: resolve_lobu_approval (packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts, around lines 600-649) is the only bridge: it reads the encrypted capability from ctx.mcpAppApprovalCapability, re-validates run/org/user/client/session/expiry, clears agentId/clientId into a "humanContext", and delegates to manageOperations approve/reject. Verify it, and check whether manage_operations is the ONLY other place that can write an approval decision, or whether there are parallel decision paths (search for other writers of interaction_status/approval events, e.g. complete_window, entity-field-approval, any route that flips a pending approval to approved/rejected).

CLAIM 4: The capability token never leaks into the model-visible surface. Verify attachMcpResultMeta in packages/server/src/tools/mcp-result-meta.ts uses a non-enumerable Symbol; then check how mcp-handler.ts consumes getMcpResultMeta (around line 484) and whether the result meta goes into the MCP response _meta field, structuredContent, formatted text, or the tool-invocation audit payload (packages/server/src/tools/audit.ts recordToolInvocationAudit). Also confirm the tool is NOT in AGENT_TOOL_NAMES/getRawDispatchTools/REST_DISPATCH_TOOL_NAMES (registry.ts MCP_APP_TOOLS comment).

CLAIM 5: Folding this into manage_operations as a normal action (capability as an ordinary arg) would expose the capability to any model that can call manage_operations and would let a model-visible call reach the approval decision. Verify whether the model can ALREADY call manage_operations approve/reject today (is manage_operations in the MCP tool list?), and what requireHumanApprovalContext would do to such a call. 

Also: hunt for COUNTEREXAMPLES to each claim (any MCP session shape with clientId null, any second approval writer, any audit/format leak of the capability, any other human-approval entry besides manage_operations approve/reject). Report them explicitly even if they are edge cases.

Final output: a numbered verdict per claim (CONFIRMED / REFUTED / PARTIAL with details), the counterexamples, and a one-paragraph bottom line on whether the separate resolve_lobu_approval tool is necessary for the human-only approval gate.

I’ll use the Lobu operator skill because this is a package-level architecture/security audit, and I’ll keep every action read-only. I’ll first load the relevant repo/memory guidance, then trace each claim and actively search for counterexamples.

The Lobu skill confirms the applicable invariants here: package guidance is authoritative, approval state must fail closed, and agent-facing versus human-only boundaries need separate tracing. Since this is analysis-only, I’m not creating a worktree or running any build/test/mutation.

The first boundary is already clear: `manage_operations` is hidden from `tools/list`, but it remains dispatchable by an MCP `tools/call` if the caller knows the name. I’m now separating OAuth, agent-bound OAuth, and PAT session shapes, because the PAT path is the likely edge case that decides whether “never” is literally true.

1. **CONFIRMED — Claim 1**

The exact gate is:

```ts
if (ctx.agentId || ctx.clientId) {
  // reject
}
if (!ctx.userId) {
  // reject
}
```

Evidence: [manage_operations.ts:2338-2352](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:2338). It runs before single approve/reject and batch approve/reject: [manage_operations.ts:2766-2773](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:2766), [manage_operations.ts:3021-3027](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:3021), [manage_operations.ts:3224-3231](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:3224), [manage_operations.ts:3313-3319](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:3313).

Caveats: these are truthiness checks, so empty-string IDs are not treated as present. The gate also does not itself inspect `isAuthenticated` or `tokenType`; it relies on a truthy `userId` plus upstream access control.

2. **REFUTED — Claim 2 as a universal statement**

For each MCP call, `mcp-handler.ts` copies the session auth context, adds host metadata, and calls `executeTool`: [mcp-handler.ts:443-455](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:443). `toToolContext` copies `userId`, `agentId`, `clientId`, token type, session ID, and capability without changing those identities: [execute.ts:388-415](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/execute.ts:388). The corresponding types permit nullable IDs: [registry.ts:93-150](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:93).

For OAuth MCP sessions, `clientId` is effectively always non-null:

- `oauth_tokens.client_id` is `NOT NULL`: [baseline.sql:1716-1729](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1716).
- Token verification returns that column as `clientId`: [provider.ts:388-416](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/auth/oauth/provider.ts:388).
- `AuthInfo.clientId` is typed as a required string: [types.ts:204-223](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/auth/oauth/types.ts:204).

An agent binding also sets `agentId`: the initialize header/body supplies `requestedAgentId` [mcp-handler.ts:627-645](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:627), and `syncAgentBinding` validates the agent and assigns it to `authCtx.agentId` [mcp-handler.ts:1038-1059](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:1038). Verified worker auth likewise supplies an agent ID: [multi-tenant.ts:352-381](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:352).

PAT nuance:

- A live PAT auth context has synthetic `clientId: pat_<id>`: [tokens.ts:113-123](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/auth/tokens.ts:113). Therefore a normal PAT MCP call is rejected by the human gate.
- The persisted `mcp_sessions.client_id` is deliberately `null` for PAT sessions because it is an OAuth-client foreign key: [mcp-handler.ts:658-669](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:658).
- That persisted null does not produce a null live `ToolContext`: recovery re-authenticates the request and retains the freshly resolved PAT context [mcp-handler.ts:747-806](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:747).

The universal claim fails because authenticated cookie-backed MCP sessions exist. That path sets a real web `session` and user but no `mcpAuthInfo` client: [multi-tenant.ts:601-628](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:601). `extractAuthContext` consequently produces `tokenType: "session"`, a session-derived `userId`, `clientId: null`, and normally `agentId: null`: [execute.ts:114-149](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/execute.ts:114). If such a session is not agent-bound, it passes `requireHumanApprovalContext`.

Therefore:

- OAuth MCP: rejected because `clientId`.
- PAT MCP: rejected because synthetic `clientId`.
- Any agent-bound MCP session: rejected because `agentId`.
- Anonymous MCP: rejected because no `userId`.
- Signed-in, unbound cookie-session MCP: can pass. This breaks “MCP can never pass.”

3. **PARTIAL — Claim 3**

The described `resolve_lobu_approval` bridge is confirmed:

- Capabilities contain run, event, org, user, client, session, and expiry, and are encrypted when issued: [mcp_app.ts:416-470](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts:416).
- The resolver decrypts the token and rechecks run/org/user/client/session/expiry: [mcp_app.ts:602-618](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts:602).
- It also verifies that the exact capability-bound event is still current and pending and rejects batched-window approvals: [mcp_app.ts:620-626](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts:620).
- Only then does it clear `agentId`, `clientId`, and the capability and delegate to canonical `manageOperations` approve/reject: [mcp_app.ts:628-648](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts:628).

For runtime human approval decisions, `manage_operations` is the canonical writer. Its builder, entity-change, and connector-operation paths perform the pending-to-approved/rejected updates: [manage_operations.ts:1961-1996](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:1961), [manage_operations.ts:2214-2245](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:2214), [manage_operations.ts:2930-2961](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:2930), [manage_operations.ts:3041-3063](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:3041). It also writes the superseding approval event and maps decision states to `interaction_status`: [manage_operations.ts:1722-1759](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations.ts:1722).

There is, however, another human-entry bridge: verified Slack entity-approval clicks construct a clientless human context and call the same `manageOperations` approve/reject actions: [interaction-bridge.ts:898-981](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/gateway/connections/interaction-bridge.ts:898). This is not a parallel writer, but it refutes “resolve_lobu_approval is the only human bridge” if interpreted system-wide.

Other apparent counterexamples are not parallel human decisions:

- `entity-field-approval.ts` creates a pending run/event and explicitly says decision orchestration lives in `manage_operations`: [entity-field-approval.ts:1-8](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts:1), [entity-field-approval.ts:785-821](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts:785).
- `complete_window` accumulates deferred proposals rather than approving them: [complete-window.ts:753-776](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_behaviors/complete-window.ts:753).
- The expiry job changes the run to `expired`, although its non-actionable UI event uses `interaction_status="rejected"`: [expire-pending-approvals.ts:146-177](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/scheduled/expire-pending-approvals.ts:146).
- Connection deletion also changes pending approvals to `expired`, not approved/rejected: [crud.ts:2085-2101](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_connections/handlers/crud.ts:2085).
- Worker completion supersedes an already-approved action’s event to completed/failed; it does not decide the approval: [run-lifecycle.ts:1878-1925](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/worker-api/run-lifecycle.ts:1878).
- A historical migration directly rejected obsolete pending `manage_watchers` rows: [20260719122000_cancel_stale_watcher_approval_runs.sql:3-22](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/db/migrations/20260719122000_cancel_stale_watcher_approval_runs.sql:3). That is a one-time data migration, not a live approval route.
- Slack has a separate `tool:*` grant/deny mechanism [interaction-bridge.ts:999-1017](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/gateway/connections/interaction-bridge.ts:999), but it operates pending tool invocations/grants rather than `runs.approval_status`.

4. **CONFIRMED — Claim 4, with an on-wire qualification**

`attachMcpResultMeta` stores metadata under a private Symbol using `enumerable: false`: [mcp-result-meta.ts:1-26](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp-result-meta.ts:1).

The capability’s destinations are:

- MCP response `_meta`: **yes**. `mcp-handler.ts` explicitly extracts the Symbol metadata and returns it as `_meta`: [mcp-handler.ts:482-515](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:482).
- `structuredContent`: **no**. Structured results are JSON-normalized, which omits the non-enumerable Symbol: [validate-args.ts:345-357](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/validate-args.ts:345).
- Formatted text/raw JSON: **no**. Formatting uses named fields or `JSON.stringify`, both of which omit the Symbol: [markdown-formatter.ts:285-313](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/formatting/markdown-formatter.ts:285), [markdown-formatter.ts:339-365](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/formatting/markdown-formatter.ts:339).
- Tool-invocation audit payload: **no**. The capability enters via request `_meta`, not `args` [mcp-handler.ts:443-451](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:443); generic audits retain sanitized arguments and status/error summaries rather than the complete result [audit.ts:175-210](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/audit.ts:175), and audit metadata does not serialize the capability-bearing context field [audit.ts:213-241](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/audit.ts:213).

The integration contract explicitly asserts that the token appears only in result `_meta`, not `structuredContent` or text: [mcp-app-resources.test.ts:786-790](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/mcp/mcp-app-resources.test.ts:786).

`resolve_lobu_approval` is app-only (`visibility: ['app']`): [registry.ts:353-373](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:353). `MCP_APP_TOOLS` are excluded from `AGENT_TOOL_NAMES`, `getAllTools`, `getRawDispatchTools`, and REST dispatch by construction: [registry.ts:333-339](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:333), [registry.ts:464-475](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:464), [registry.ts:705-717](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:705). The registry test specifically confirms it is not REST-dispatchable: [tool-registry-split.test.ts:84-93](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/__tests__/unit/tool-registry-split.test.ts:84).

Qualification: the encrypted capability is present on the MCP wire in response `_meta`; the “never model-visible” property relies on a conforming host preserving the MCP `_meta` model/app boundary. A malicious or non-conforming host could expose wire metadata to its model.

5. **PARTIAL — Claim 5**

`manage_operations` is **not advertised directly** in MCP `tools/list`. Admin tools are placed in `INTERNAL_DISPATCH_TOOLS`, which are callable by name but omitted from the listed MCP set: [registry.ts:413-466](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:413). The MCP handler’s comment and listing construction confirm that split: [mcp-handler.ts:338-381](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:338).

Nevertheless, the same handler is model-reachable in two ways:

- A caller that knows the hidden name may send `tools/call` directly; the handler dispatches arbitrary registered names through `executeTool`: [mcp-handler.ts:443-455](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:443).
- The advertised `run_sdk` surface exposes `client.operations.approve/reject`; those methods directly wrap `manageOperations`: [operations.ts:25-98](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/sandbox/namespaces/operations.ts:25). They are explicitly model-discoverable write methods: [method-metadata.ts:837-844](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/sandbox/method-metadata.ts:837).

Today, an OAuth/PAT/agent model call reaches the handler but is rejected by `requireHumanApprovalContext`. The signed-in unbound cookie-session MCP counterexample can pass.

Moving the capability into ordinary arguments would move it from the host-only `_meta` channel into the ordinary caller-authored argument channel. That would allow any model-visible path possessing the token to present it to the canonical approval handler. However, “it would expose the actual token to every model” is not inevitable from the schema change alone: `manage_operations` is not directly listed, and actual exposure would depend on how the host/widget injected that argument. The security-boundary concern is valid, but the categorical exposure wording is stronger than current code proves.

**Counterexamples found:** authenticated unbound cookie MCP sessions can have `userId` with null `clientId`/`agentId`; PAT session rows persist a null client ID but live PAT contexts do not; Slack is a second verified-human bridge into `manage_operations`; expiry produces a rejected-looking interaction event without a human rejection; historical migrations can directly reject obsolete rows; and MCP `_meta` is host-only but still present on the wire.

Bottom line: the separate `resolve_lobu_approval` tool is necessary for the current OAuth MCP App design because ordinary OAuth/model calls necessarily carry `clientId` and fail the canonical human gate, while the app-only resolver can validate a hidden, encrypted, user/client/session-bound click capability before clearing the transport identities and invoking the one canonical decision writer. It also keeps that exception out of agent, REST, OpenAPI, and ClientSDK surfaces. It is not sufficient to support the absolute statement “MCP can never approve,” because an authenticated, unbound cookie-session MCP context already satisfies the gate and can reach `manage_operations` directly or through `run_sdk`.
